content:
The concept of Extension Bloat has moved from a niche tech complaint to a major performance bottleneck in 2026. While a fresh Chromium install is lean and fast, a "daily driver" often suffers from resource fragmentation, where dozens of extensions compete for CPU cycles and memory, even when not in use. This research-backed guide covers Extension Bloat: Why Your 'Clean' Chromium Install Is Faster Than Your Daily Driver.

Recent Research & Articles (2025–2026)

1. arXiv – Impact of Extensions on Browser Performance

An empirical study quantifying how even inactive extensions increase page load times and energy consumption.

2. ResearchGate – Slimium: Debloating the Chromium Browser

Slimium analyzes how "feature subsetting" can remove bloated dependencies that slow down the Chromium core.

3. Malwarebytes – "Sleeper" Extensions Woke Up as Spyware

Malwarebytes details how "clean" extensions become bloated with malicious code via background updates years after installation.

4. How-To Geek – Why Chrome Is Still My Default in 2025

How-To Geek explores the "clutter" of modern Chromium, including AI features and side-panels that contribute to a bloated UI.

5. Medium – Chrome Is Eating Your RAM: A Registry Fix

Medium discusses the "Chrome RAM Eater" meme and how background extension processes destabilize system performance.

Core Challenges & Problems

  • The Manifest V3 Paradox: Google moved to Manifest V3 (MV3) to improve performance by forcing service workers to sleep, but many developers struggled to optimize. This led to "zombie processes" that fail to terminate, keeping RAM occupied.
  • Sleeper Agents & Update Bloat: In 2025, legitimate extensions were sold to new developers who pushed updates containing tracking scripts and adware, turning a once-lean utility into a resource-heavy "sleeper agent."
  • Process Isolation Overhead: Chromium assigns a separate process to every extension. Twenty extensions mean 20+ extra background processes. A fresh install (0 extensions) has zero overhead, hence the "day one" speed advantage.
